title: LRU cache with TTL where the rules interact
prompt:
Write `cache.py` in this workspace containing a class `Cache` -- an LRU cache with a time-to-live. There is an existing `tests/test_cache.py`; it covers the basics only and passing it is NOT sufficient.

`Cache(capacity, ttl_seconds, now=time.monotonic)`. `now` is a zero-argument callable returning a float, injected so tests control time; default to `time.monotonic`. An entry is EXPIRED when `now() - (the time it was last written) >= ttl_seconds`.

The rules, all of which must hold together:

1. `put(key, value)`: insert, or update an existing key. Either way the entry becomes the most-recently-used AND its TTL clock RESETS (an update makes it fresh again).
2. `get(key)`: return the value, or None if the key is absent or expired. A `get` that finds an EXPIRED entry must REMOVE that entry and must NOT change recency ordering -- it is not a use.
3. A `get` that returns a live value DOES make that entry the most-recently-used.
4. Expired entries must never occupy capacity. When `put` needs room, it must first drop every expired entry; only if the cache is still full does it evict.
5. Eviction removes the least-recently-used entry among entries that are still LIVE.
6. `len(cache)` counts LIVE entries only -- never expired ones still held internally.
7. `keys()` returns the live keys in order, least-recently-used first.

Use only the standard library.
